newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Napocor says no power rate hike this month.
newsitem.headline: Manila Napocor says no power rate hike this month.

text.p: The Philippines' National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Monday it will not raise power rates this month despite the recent increase in local petroleum product prices.
Napocor president Guido Delgado said in a statement rates in August will be based on fuel prices and the power generation mix in July.
Last August 1, the country's three oil refiners - Petron Corp, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, and Caltex (Philippines) Inc - raised rates of all petroleum products.
Fuel oil was raised by 22 centavos per litre while diesel oil was increased by 10 centavos a litre.
Delgado said Napocor will lower the use of fuel oil and diesel in the power generation mix to cushion the impact of the oil price increases.

He said that Napocor had managed to reduce the share of fuel oil in the generation mix to 39 percent of the generation mix in since the oil price hike from an average of 51 percent the first six months of the year.
"If we are able to maintain our current generation mix persists for the remainder of August, then any movement in the September power rates will only be minimal," Delgado added.
